correctness.rationale: For all integers N≥2 and all positive normalized fixed unoriented planar directions, derived the worst-body perimeter-normalized Cauchy quadrature error E(µ)=½ max{2/π−rµ,Rµ−2/π} from the planar surface-area integral; thin rectangles realize the sup norm. The associated symmetric zonogon Z=∑w[-u,u] has perimeter 4. A tangential m-gon bounded by its 2k≤2N facet normals and origin-centered inradius r gives 2r∑tan(Δ_i/2)≤4; Jensen and monotonicity of m tan(π/m) yield r≤cot(π/(2N))/N=rN. Equality forces all Δ_i=π/N and regular Z and equal weights. The regular N-rule has R=1/(N sin(π/(2N))) and R+rN<4/π, making the lower discrepancy sharp and E_N=π^{-1}(1−x cot x), x=π/(2N). The global strict-convexity tangent deficit yields ∑(Δ_i−π/N)^2≤24δ/[x rN(rN−2δ)] for 0≤δ<rN/2; ≤48δ/(x rN²) for δ≤rN/4. A symmetric ±t gap deformation has δ=c_N t²+O(t⁴), so angular deviation scales as √δ. Independently evaluated small-N exact formulas and numerical perturbed geometry; these are corroboration, not the all-N proof.
